clue.text: Mother and aunt wandering round Italian city

parts.note: MA is a familiar word for mother

indicators.note: letters wandering round end up in a fresh order, so the word aunt is rearranged

explanation.surface: A mother and her aunt get lost touring an Italian city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' looks like part of the touring picture but belongs to the anagram signal 'wandering round', which scrambles only the aunt.
explanation.definitionFit: Mantua (Mantova) is a historic city in Lombardy, northern Italy.

clue.text: Illness cramping student's vocal style

indicators.note: to cramp something is to hem it in, so the illness word encloses the student's letter

parts.note: an infection is an illness
L is the learner plate letter, standing for a student

explanation.surface: Being ill spoils a student's singing voice.
explanation.definitionFit: Inflection is modulation of the voice in pitch or tone, a speaker's vocal manner.

clue.text: Help a gas to be released as industrial waste

indicators.note: letters released from their order are free to form a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Someone calls for help as gas escapes from a factory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be released' rearranges the letters of HELP A GAS.
explanation.definitionFit: A slag heap is a mound of mining or smelting spoil, a classic form of industrial refuse.

clue.text: Ruction as brother's taken in by a fairy

indicators.note: the brother's letters are taken inside the fairy word

parts.note: a fay is a poetic word for a fairy
Fr is the abbreviation for Brother (or Father) in a religious order

explanation.surface: A sibling is duped by a fairy, causing a commotion.
explanation.definitionFit: An affray is a noisy public brawl, so a ruction or disturbance.

clue.text: When without underwear, compiler's been apt to cause friction

indicators.note: in the old sense of outside, so the when-word sits outside the underwear

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as I left'
a bra is an item of underwear
the setter speaking as I: I have been is shortened to I've

explanation.surface: The setter confesses that going without underwear chafed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' is used in its old sense of outside, not lacking. Setters often call themselves 'compiler', so 'compiler's been' means the setter has been.
explanation.definitionFit: Something abrasive rubs and wears, so it tends to cause friction, literally or socially.

clue.text: Desperately short of love, indeed

indicators.note: something done desperately is frantic and disordered, so these letters are scrambled

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, which looks like the letter O

explanation.surface: Someone is in dire need of romance, truly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Desperately' shuffles SHORT, OF and O (love) together.
explanation.definitionFit: Forsooth is an archaic interjection meaning in truth or truly.

clue.text: Accompanying to the finish in the finish

indicators.note: one finish word is placed inside the other

parts.note: the end is the finish
the close is the finish, as of a day

explanation.surface: A runner is escorted right up to the end line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to the finish' reads like a phrase about going all the way, but the first 'the finish' is wordplay and 'to' only links it to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An item enclosed with a letter accompanies it in the same envelope.

clue.text: Power rock

definitions.meaning: ... means influence or control, as in holding ...

explanation.definitionFit: Sway is both a noun meaning dominion and a verb meaning to swing gently back and forth.

clue.text: Brought up a little bit of information

indicators.note: in a down light, bringing a word up reads it from the bottom, so backwards

parts.note: a tad is a little bit

explanation.surface: Someone raised a scrap of news.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry 'Brought up' reverses only the little bit; the plain 'a' then follows it.
explanation.definitionFit: Data are facts and figures, a general word for information.

clue.text: Right cultured, holding one distinctive piece

indicators.note: the cultured word holds the one letter inside it

parts.note: arty means pretentiously cultured or artistic
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A properly refined person holds onto one unusual item.
explanation.definitionFit: A rarity is an uncommon object, something distinctive because seldom seen.

clue.text: Shameless patriotic diatribe?

parts.note: the flag is the emblem of patriotism, so a patriotic speech is whimsically a flag one
a rant is a diatribe

explanation.surface: An unashamed nationalist harangue.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the whimsical reading: a patriotic diatribe would be a flag-waving rant.
explanation.definitionFit: Flagrant means conspicuously offensive, done openly and without shame.

clue.text: Second book, including two German cries of pain

indicators.note: the book word includes the cries inside it

parts.note: a tome is a large book

indicators.note: two copies of the cry are wanted

parts.note: ach is a German exclamation, alas or oh

explanation.surface: A second volume contains a couple of Teutonic wails of anguish.
explanation.definitionFit: Stomach ache is a specific pain, an ache in the belly.

clue.text: Grant to house woman on the brink, going round the bend

parts.note: Nora is a woman's name

indicators.note: the brink word goes round the bend letter, enclosing it

parts.note: a rim is a brink or edge
a U-bend is a bend shaped like the letter U, so U stands for a bend

explanation.surface: A grant to give a home to a woman who is on the edge and losing her mind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going round the bend' looks like madness, but it is a container signal; 'on' is only a link placing the woman before the brink. A U-bend gives U for bend.
explanation.definitionFit: An honorarium is a voluntary payment for services, a grant in recognition rather than a fee.

clue.text: Crosby's to fall in, breaking head

indicators.note: the fall word goes inside the crooner's first name

parts.note: Bing Crosby was the American crooner
to rain is to fall from the sky

explanation.surface: Crosby is about to fall in and crack his head.
explanation.definitionFit: Braining someone means striking their head hard, so breaking their head.

clue.text: Dish containing yam cooked by childhood friend

indicators.note: the dish word contains the other letters

parts.note: a plate is a dish

indicators.note: cooking changes the form of something, so yam is rearranged

explanation.surface: A plate holds a yam prepared by a childhood companion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cooked' scrambles the yam only, and the result goes inside the dish; 'by' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A playmate is a friend one plays with, especially as a child.

clue.text: Source of health and energy keeping volunteers in

indicators.note: the energy word keeps the other letters inside

parts.note: vim is energy or vigour
TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve force

explanation.surface: Something healthy and energising that keeps the reservists going.
explanation.walkthrough: TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's part-time volunteer reserve.
explanation.definitionFit: A vitamin is a nutrient that sustains health, so a source of wellbeing.

clue.text: Den and Tim are upset about Bob's faulty hearing

indicators.note: the reversed words go about the coin letter
in a down light, upset means turned upside down, reading both words from the bottom

parts.note: a lair is a den
a bob was a shilling in old British money, abbreviated s

explanation.surface: Two men are annoyed at Bob for mishearing them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'are upset' reverses the den and Tim together as one run; 'about' then puts the old shilling letter inside it. A bob was a pre-decimal British shilling.
explanation.definitionFit: A mistrial is a trial invalidated by error, so a faulty court hearing.

clue.text: Threaten scamp, getting old money back

parts.note: an imp is a mischievous child, a scamp

indicators.note: back means the money word is read in reverse

parts.note: lire were Italy's currency before the euro

explanation.surface: Someone menaces a rascal to get their old money returned.
explanation.definitionFit: To imperil something is to put it in danger, so to threaten it.

clue.text: Swim in peace, making happy finds

indicators.note: the swim word is placed in the peace word

parts.note: serenity is peace and calm
a dip is a short swim

explanation.surface: A tranquil bathe leads to lucky discoveries.
explanation.definitionFit: Serendipity is the knack of stumbling on fortunate discoveries by chance.

clue.text: One famous tenor almost a failure as an aviator

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: almost the whole name, so its last letter is cut

parts.note: Enrico Caruso was the celebrated Italian tenor

explanation.surface: A great tenor who nearly flopped at flying.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth Icarus flew too near the sun on wax wings and fell, the archetypal failed flyer.

clue.text: The story of a piece of land

definitions.meaning: the storyline of a novel or film

explanation.surface: The history of a small field.
explanation.definitionFit: Plot means both a narrative's sequence of events and a small measured area of land.

clue.text: Far from stern stalk

definitions.meaning: a ship's bow, the opposite end from the stern

explanation.definitionFit: Stem names both the prow of a ship and the main stalk of a plant.

clue.text: Dubious retail lines in books

indicators.note: dubious means unreliable or shady, so the letters of retail are suspect and rearranged

parts.note: RY is the abbreviation for railway, lines of track

explanation.surface: Questionable shop trade in printed books.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dubious' scrambles only the retail; railway lines, abbreviated, are added at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Literary means concerning literature, so found in or relating to books.

clue.text: Piece of excrement in a film

parts.note: a cowpat is a lump of dung, so pat is a piece of excrement

explanation.surface: A bit of dung appears in a movie.
explanation.definitionFit: A patina is a thin surface film, such as the green coating on old bronze.

clue.text: Tummy pain one ignored, beating drum

indicators.note: ignored means the one letter is left out of the pool
beating a mixture churns it, so the remaining letters are rearranged

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: An aching stomach throbs like a drum.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ignored' drops I from TUMMY PAIN; 'beating' rearranges the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: The tympanum is the eardrum, and also a term for a drum or drumhead.

clue.text: Rob King's piercing instrument

indicators.note: the king's letter pierces the instrument word, going inside it

parts.note: a bugle is a brass instrument
R stands for Rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A king's instrument makes a shrill sound.
explanation.definitionFit: To burgle is to break into a building and steal, so to rob.
